premises: Nanohierarchical architecture with nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates can be engineered in a high-entropy alloy.
This architecture activates an adaptive friction interface protection mechanism.
The mechanism releases gradient frictional stress at room temperature and forms a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer at 800 °C.
The adaptive mechanism concurrently reduces coefficient of friction and wear rate.
The effect is effective over a wide temperature range (RT to 800 °C).
